sentences: Should you defrag your S S D?
On a hard drive, a file can end up in scattered pieces.
The read head has to jump across the spinning platter to reach each one.
Defragging puts them back in a row.
An S S D has no moving parts.
It reads flash chips electronically, so a file in one piece or fifty pieces loads at almost the same speed.
Defragging would rewrite lots of data for nothing.
Flash cells survive a limited number of writes, so that just wears the drive out.
On an S S D, Optimize Drives sends a TRIM command instead, telling the drive which blocks are free.
Why hard drives hate scattered files is in our video, S S D versus H D D versus N V M e.
